title: Engineered Vascularized Muscle Flap
protocol: Dissolve 500 mg of PLLA and 500 mg of PLGA in 10 ml chloroform.
Add 0.24 ml of polymer solution to 0.4 g of sodium chloride particles gathered in a Teflon mold with a salt diameter of 212-600 µm.
Allow the chloroform to evaporate overnight.
Leach the salt out using distilled water leading to interconnected porous 3D scaffolds.
Cut polymer pieces using scissors.
Soak scaffold pieces in 70% ethanol (v/v) for 30 min.
Wash scaffold pieces three times in PBS for 2 min before usage.
Prepare a tri-culture of cells consisting of 0.5 x 10^6 C2C12 myoblasts, 0.9 x 10^6 Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), and 0.2 x 10^6 Normal human dermal fibroblasts (NHDF).

Culture the cells in a mixture of equal parts endothelial cell medium (EGM-2 supplemented with bullet kit components) and muscle cell medium (DMEM, supplemented with 10% FBS, 2.5% HEPES buffer, 100 U/ml penicillin, and 0.1 mg/ml streptomycin).
Mix the cells together in a microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 200 x g for 4 min.
Aspirate the medium and re-suspend the pellet in a mixture of 4 μl ice cold extracellular matrix solution and 4 μl cell medium.
Cut a piece of PLLA/PLGA scaffold measuring 10 mm x 7 mm x 1 mm (length x width x thickness).
Seed the cell suspension on the scaffold in a 6-well plate.
Allow the extracellular matrix solution to solidify at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Add 4 ml of cell medium after solidification.
Incubate the scaffolds for ten days before implantation.
Replace the medium every other day.
Prepare and sterilize (autoclave) a small, fine, straight scissors.
Prepare and sterilize (autoclave) a spring scissors.
Prepare and sterilize (autoclave) a straight, fine-tipped forceps.
Prepare and sterilize (autoclave) a serrated forceps.
Prepare and sterilize (autoclave) a needle holder.
Mix 425 µl ketamine with 75 µl xylazine in a 1 ml syringe to prepare the anesthesia solution.
Dilute 0.3 mg/ml buprenorphine in sterile saline at a ratio of 1:20.
Anesthetize the mouse by intraperitoneal injection of ketamine:xylazine (35 µl per 20 g of body weight).
Subcutaneously inject buprenorphine at a final concentration of 0.05-0.1 mg/kg before the operation.
Place the mouse on a stage heated to 37 °C to maintain normal body temperature.
Secure the mouse using an adhesive bandage.
Administer lubricating eye ointment subcutaneously in the eyes with cotton tips (to prevent dehydration).
Clean the incision site with iodine using cotton tips.
Clean the incision site with 70% ethanol using cotton tips.
Make an incision through the skin from the knee level to the inguinal ligament, parallel to the femoral vessels, until the femoral artery and vein are exposed.
Hold the skin down using a retractor for better access to the tissue.
Isolate the femoral artery and vein from surrounding tissue starting at the inguinal ligament to the superior epigastric vessel bifurcation.
Wrap the graft around the exposed femoral AV, below the profunda and above the tibial and proneal AV bifurcation.
Join the ends of the graft using 8-0 silk sutures.
Wrap a piece of sterilized latex around the graft to ensure implant vascularization by capillary sprouting from the femoral AV vessels.
Suture the wrapped graft with 6-0 sutures.
Close the overlying skin using 4-0 silk sutures.
Monitor the mouse closely until recovery from anesthesia and every day thereafter, until the graft is transferred as a flap.
Subcutaneously inject buprenorphine at a final concentration of 0.05-0.1 mg/kg twice a day for 2-3 days.
Anesthetize the mouse by an intraperitoneal injection of ketamine:xylazine (35 µl/20 g).
Subcutaneously inject buprenorphine (final concentration of 0.05-0.1 mg/kg) before the operation.
Place the mouse on a stage heated to 37 °C.
Secure the mouse using an adhesive bandage.
Apply lubricating eye ointment to the mouse's eyes.
Clean the incision site with iodine and then with 70% ethanol.
Open the sutures in the skin using scissors and forceps.
Make an incision through the skin parallel to the inguinal ligament.
Carefully remove the latex piece with forceps and expose the vascularized flap.
Dissect the tissue flap from the surrounding tissue.
Ligate the distal end of the femoral AV with 8-0 silk sutures.
Cauterize the AV at the level of the knee, distally to the folded implanted tissue and the 8-0 sutures.
Gently transfer the femoral AV enveloped by the graft towards the ventral abdominal wall.
Using a fine scissors, make an incision in the ventral abdominal wall.
Using a spring scissors, make an incision in the rectus abdominus muscle.
Remove an approximately 1 cm x 0.8 cm segment of the rectus abdominus muscle with the overlying skin.
Transfer the femoral AV, enveloped by the vascularized graft, as an axial flap, to the full-thickness defect in the ventral abdominal wall.
Suture the flap to the surrounding muscle tissue, using 8-0 silk sutures, to prevent hernia.
To avoid suturing the internal organs, raise the muscle with a forceps when suturing the flap to the abdominal muscle.
Leave the ventral skin exposed to mimic the effect of a full abdominal wall defect.
Cover the wound in the skin with iodinated gauze and a sterile bandage to prevent contamination of the exposed area.
Suture the skin of the leg using 4-0 silk sutures.
Monitor the mouse closely until recovery from the anesthesia and every day thereafter, until retrieval of the flap.
Subcutaneously inject buprenorphine (final concentration of 0.05-0.1 mg/kg) twice a day for 2-3 days.
Anesthetize the mouse using 2% isoflurane before transfer.
Place the mouse on a movable stage heated to 38 °C.
Secure the mouse using an adhesive bandage.
Find the femoral artery and vein vessels with a non-linear transducer set on B-mode.
Examine the patency of the femoral vessels of the graft using the transducer set on color Doppler mode.
Prepare non-targeted contrast agent according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Connect a tail vein catheter (12 cm tubing with a 27 G needle) to a 1 ml syringe filled with saline.
Secure the syringe next to the mouse on the heating stage.
Connect the catheter to the mouse tail vein and secure the needle.
Inject some of the saline to ensure that injections are being made into the vein and to fill the tubing with saline.
Fill a 1 ml syringe with 70 µl of contrast agent and replace the saline syringe with the contrast agent syringe.
Set up the ultrasound to image injection of the contrast agent.
In properties of the non-linear mode set up the number of frames to 1,500.
Set the disruption pulse to 30% of the frames.
Slowly inject the contrast agent into the tail vein.
Capture images in the non-linear contrast mode of the high-resolution ultrasound system.
Draw a region of interest (ROI) on the image obtained immediately after the disruption pulse in the contrast-mode.

Calculate the peak enhancement (PE), which is the ratio of the mean intensity of the non-linear signal after the injection of the microbubbles versus after the disruption pulse, and is a measure of the perfusion volume.
Calculate the flow rate, which is determined from the time that elapses until the peak signal.
Anesthetize the mouse by an intraperitoneal injection of ketamine:xylazine (35 µl/20 g) using an insulin syringe.
Intravenously inject 200 μl of 10 mg/ml fluorescein isothiocyanate-conjugated dextran into the tail vein using a 1 ml syringe.
Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation ten seconds after completion of the injection.
Open the leg of the mouse and expose the graft.
Wash the graft area with phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Apply 10% neutral buffered formalin to the graft area.
Image the graft in the mouse leg using a confocal microscope.
Quantify functional vessel density (FVD).
Isolate the green channel (excitation = 488 nm) of the confocal microscopic images.
Pass the resulting images through a high-pass filter to accentuate high-contrast structures.
Use a despeckling filter to remove noise amplified by the high-pass filter.
Set up the threshold value on the resulting image for visibility in binary form.
Apply a size-threshold so that only groups of connected pixels larger than the defined size remain.
Outline the skeleton of the vessels using the Zhang-Suen's algorithm.
Calculate the FVD by summing the lengths of the midline of each vessel and dividing by the area of the ROI.
Retrieve the graft using small scissors and forceps after confocal imaging.
Dissect the AV vessels at both ends of the graft to retrieve it.
Fix the grafts in 10% neutral buffered formalin for 30 min - 2 hr.
Place the fixed grafts in histology cassettes.
Store the grafts in 70% ethanol until paraffin embedding.
Embed the grafts in paraffin using a standard fixation and embedding protocol.
Slice the paraffin-embedded tissues into 5 µm slices using a microtome.
Slice the tissue perpendicularly to the AV vessels.
Deparaffinize the paraffin-embedded sections by immersion in 100% xylene twice, for 10 min each.
Rehydrate the slides by serial immersions in decreasing concentrations of ethanol (100%, 96%, 90%, 80%, 70%, 50%, 30%) and double distilled water (DDW), for 3 min each.
Dilute 2.35 ml of antigen unmasking solution with 250 mL of DDW to prepare the antigen unmasking solution.
Heat the prepared antigen unmasking solution for 2 min in a microwave set to 95 °C.
Insert the slides into the pre-heated antigen unmasking solution and heat again for 3 min at 95 °C.
Cool the slides to 50 °C.
Heat the slides again for 2 min, then cool them to room temperature (RT).
Incubate the slides in a 3.3% H2O2 solution in methanol for 10 min at RT.
Rinse the slides twice with PBS after incubation.
Prepare an incubation chamber: place wet absorbent sheets inside a histology box and dry the slides using delicate task wipers.
Circle the slice area on each slide using a hydrophobic pen.
Incubate the slides for 30 min at RT, applying approximately 50 μl of goat serum blocking solution (2%, prepared in PBS) per slice.
Dilute the rabbit anti-CD31 antibody 1:50 in blocking solution and apply approximately 50 μl antibody per slice; incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Rinse the slides three times with PBS, for 5 min each.
Dilute the biotinylated goat anti-rabbit secondary antibody 1:400 in PBS and place over the slides approximately 50 μl of antibody per slice; incubate for 30 min at RT.
Rinse the slides three times with PBS, for 5 min each.
Dilute streptavidin-peroxidase 1:400 in PBS.
Apply approximately 50 µl per slice and incubate with slides for 30 min at room temperature.
Rinse slices 3 times with PBS, each for 5 min.
Apply approximately 50 µl of aminoethylcarbazole (AEC) substrate per slice according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Dip the slides in distilled deionized water to stop the reaction.
Stain nuclei in blue by immersing the sections in approximately 50 µl of Mayer’s hematoxylin solution for 2 min.
Gently rinse sections in water and then cover with mounting medium.
Quantify CD31-positive staining using a double-blind approach.
Choose 4-5 different fields in a 40X magnification viewing field under a binocular microscope.
Count the number of CD31-positive lumens.
Calculate the average number of CD31-positive lumens per scaffold by dividing the total number of counted lumens with the number of fields and the field area.
Fix grafts in 10% neutral buffered formalin.
Embed grafts in paraffin using standard fixation and embedding procedures.
Remove the paraffin from the paraffin-embedded sections by immersion in 100% xylene twice for 10 min each.
Fast wash twice for rehydration in 100% isopropanol.
Fast wash twice with 95% ethanol.
Wash three times in tap water.
Immerse sections in Hematoxylin for 10 min.
Wash three times in tap water.
Immersion in Eosin for 2 min.
Fast wash dehydrate in 95% Ethanol twice.
Fast wash in 100% isopropanol twice.
Fast wash in 100% xylene twice.
Cover with DPX glue using a cover glass 1.5 mm thick.
Image the sample using a microscope at 40X magnification.
Retrieve the graft using small scissors and forceps.
Rinse the graft in PBS.
Measure the width and thickness of the graft to calculate the cross-sectional area.
Mount the graft between system tensile grips, measuring the initial length.
Apply strain rate of 0.01 mm/sec until failure is achieved.
Record developed force and displacement according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Generate a stress-strain curve in Matlab.
Calculate strain as displacement divided by the initial length.
Determine stress as measured force divided by cross-sectional area.
Identify stiffness as slope of linear region in the stress-strain curve.
Determine ultimate tensile strength from the maximum point on the stress-strain curve.
